catalog_name: TGAI Curated Open Model Catalog v0005
notes: Expanded public curation for the TGAI Browser LLM Lab. The live WebLLM prebuilt catalog remains authoritative for direct browser loadability. This catalog separates browser-loadable MLC/WebLLM experiments from reference-only local-desktop models and image-generation runtimes. Embedding models are retained for future semantic retrieval/RAG but are not chat models. Qwen3-Coder 30B and Qwen3.5 coding variants are intentionally reference-only: they are strong local coding-workstation candidates for Ollama/llama.cpp-class runtimes, not models TGAI should imply are directly browser-loadable.

models.good_for_text: Excellent experimental baseline for SQL, PL/SQL, JavaScript, code transformation, and grounded domain assistants. Small enough to show how much authoritative reference material can compensate for model size.
A particularly interesting next step for TGAI: stronger coding/SQL capacity than 0.5B while still much smaller than 7B. Good candidate for grounded Oracle EBS work and everyday code review.
Strong candidate for the middle ground between browser speed and coding quality. Worth benchmarking on Oracle EBS SQL both with and without local grounding.

models.display_name: Qwen2.5 Coder 7B q4f32 · Heavy Coding Control
models.good_for_text: Large coding control model. Useful for measuring quality gains versus smaller grounded models, but on modest GPUs it can be far too slow for interactive work; your first TGAI test measured about 0.74 tokens/sec.
General-purpose small instruction model for writing, summarization, extraction, Q&A, and comparing a generalist against the Coder variant at a similar size.
Very small model useful for testing low-resource browser inference, simple extraction, short rewriting, and the limits of tiny grounded assistants.
Lightweight general instruction model for chat, summarization, rewriting, and comparison with similarly sized Qwen/Phi models.
Compact higher-capability model worth testing for reasoning, technical Q&A, writing, extraction, and code tasks when a tiny model is not enough.

models.display_name: Phi-3.5 Vision q4f16 · Image Understanding Lab
models.good_for_text: IMAGE → TEXT model. Official WebLLM config estimates about 3.95 GB VRAM. TGAI v0014 downsamples images before sending them; still treat this as a heavy experimental workload on integrated graphics.
General-purpose 3B Llama control for comparing grounded behavior against Qwen and Phi models.
Large general instruction model for broader chat, writing, summarization, and reasoning comparisons. More demanding than 1–3B browser models.

models.display_name: DeepSeek R1 Distill Qwen 7B · Reasoning Experiment
models.good_for_text: Interesting for deliberate multi-step reasoning, analytical problem solving, and code/math experiments. Expect a substantially heavier browser workload than small instruction models.
Compact Microsoft Phi-family model for technical Q&A, reasoning, writing, summarization and code experiments. Useful comparison against Qwen Coder and Llama in the middle-size browser tier.
General-purpose 3B Qwen control for writing, extraction, summarization and technical Q&A; useful against the specialized Qwen Coder 3B.
Large general-purpose Qwen model for capability comparisons on stronger hardware. Expect a major memory and speed cost in browser inference.
High-memory 7B experiment with much less aggressive weight quantization than q4. Interesting for fidelity comparisons on a machine with substantial GPU/shared memory.
8B general-purpose control with a reduced 1K context configuration intended to lower resource requirements. Better for short prompts than document-heavy grounding.
Instruction-tuned Mistral-family experiment useful for structured responses, general assistant work and comparing behavior with base Mistral/Qwen/Llama families.

models.display_name: Stable Diffusion 2.1 Base ONNX · Browser Text-to-Image Research
models.good_for_text: PROMPT → IMAGE legacy compatibility reference. TGAI can load this ONNX export, including its split VAE external data, but current ORT WebGPU/Edge/Dawn testing reaches the U-Net and then fails when the BiasSplitGelu WebGPU shader is rejected. Retained as a useful compatibility case, not a recommended image-generation path.
PROMPT → IMAGE research candidate. ONNX Stable Diffusion pipelines exist, but this is not loadable through WebLLM; TGAI would need a dedicated diffusion pipeline/runtime.
Very small Qwen3-family experiment. Attractive for testing how much capability TGAI can recover from strong grounding on constrained hardware.
Modern Qwen3 middle-small model. A particularly interesting TGAI candidate between tiny models and the 3–4B class.
Stronger Qwen3 experiment for reasoning and general technical work. Likely substantially heavier than the 1.7B model on this machine.
Higher-memory Qwen3 4B control for quantization comparisons. Not a first choice on constrained integrated graphics.
Heavy Qwen3 capability control. Included for catalog completeness, but likely beyond the comfortable interactive range of the current machine.
Compact Llama-family control for grounded writing, extraction and simple technical work; a useful comparison with Qwen3 0.6B/1.7B.
Extremely small baseline for speed and grounding experiments. Useful for testing the minimum viable local model size.
Older lightweight Llama-family control. Less compelling than newer small models, but useful as a historical/browser performance baseline.

models.display_name: Phi-2 q4f16 · Legacy Compact Reasoning Control
models.good_for_text: Older compact Phi-family model for historical comparison. Newer Phi/Qwen models are generally more interesting for new TGAI work.
Small Gemma 3 instruction model. Interesting family-diversity comparison if it appears in the live WebLLM catalog.
Modern 4B Gemma-family model. Included as a researched MLC/WebLLM candidate; TGAI will only mark it loadable if the live WebLLM catalog contains the matching record.
Very heavy Gemma 3 research control. Cataloged for completeness, not recommended on the current machine.
Instruction/tool-oriented 8B control found in the broader MLC web-llm-tagged catalog. Heavy for current hardware.

models.display_name: Phi-3.5 Vision q4f32 · Very Heavy Vision Control
models.good_for_text: Higher-memory IMAGE → TEXT control. Official WebLLM config estimates about 5.88 GB VRAM; not recommended for the current machine after the q4f16 freeze.
Small math-specialized Qwen2.5 model. Useful for quantitative reasoning experiments; WebLLM's current prebuilt config lists this q4f16 variant at about 1.63 GB VRAM.
Compact instruction/chat control with a 1K context configuration. Current WebLLM config estimates about 1.51 GB VRAM.
Compact StableLM-family chat model with larger context than the 1K variant; useful as a non-Qwen small-model comparison.
Very small chat model; WebLLM's current config estimates about 697 MB VRAM. Useful as a minimum-capability baseline against newer Qwen3/SmolLM models.
Older 3B chat baseline with reduced context. Current WebLLM config lists about 2.04 GB VRAM and requires shader-f16.

models.display_name: DeepSeek R1 Distill Llama 8B · Heavy Reasoning Control
models.good_for_text: Heavy reasoning model. Current WebLLM prebuilt config lists roughly 5.0 GB VRAM. Cataloged for comparison, but not recommended for the current machine.

models.display_name: Hermes 2 Theta Llama 3 8B · Heavy Instruction Control
models.good_for_text: Instruction-tuned Llama 3 family control. Current WebLLM config lists about 4.98 GB VRAM; too heavy for routine use on the current machine.
A more aggressively quantized Mistral 7B package. The MLC repository is about 3.28 GB, smaller than its q4 package, but still a heavy browser workload.
Small Gemma 3 instruction model packaged by MLC for WebLLM/MLC-LLM. Interesting modern family comparison if present in the live WebLLM catalog.
Modern Gemma 3 4B MLC/WebLLM package. Potentially interesting on stronger hardware; TGAI only marks it directly loadable when your live WebLLM build exposes it.

models.display_name: Snowflake Arctic Embed S · Local Retrieval / RAG Model
models.good_for_text: Embedding model, not a chatbot. Converts text into vectors for semantic similarity, document retrieval and a future local RAG pipeline. TGAI v0015 disables normal chat when it is loaded.

models.display_name: SD-Turbo ORT Web · Fast Browser Image Baseline
models.good_for_text: PROMPT → IMAGE browser-local baseline proven in TGAI. Fast 1–4 pass generation with deterministic seeds and browser disk caching. Best used as the lightweight image-generation control.

models.display_name: SDXL-Lightning Q4 · Higher-Quality Browser Image Model
models.good_for_text: PROMPT → IMAGE higher-quality TGAI path. Uses SDXL dual text encoders, pooled conditioning/time IDs, quantized Lightning U-Net and split external ONNX weights. Heavier than SD-Turbo but proven end-to-end in the browser lab.

REFERENCE-ONLY for TGAI browser use. Serious local coding-workstation candidate: 30.5B total parameters with about 3.3B activated, native 256K context, tool/function-call oriented agentic coding, and repository-scale use. Ollama's Q4_K_M package is about 19 GB, making this a desktop-runtime target rather than a practical current browser target.

models.display_name: Qwen3-Coder 30B Q4 · Ollama Local Coding Reference
models.good_for_text: REFERENCE-ONLY local runtime package for a coding workstation. Ollama lists the Q4_K_M build at roughly 19 GB with a 256K context window. Attractive for pairing with Open WebUI, OpenCode, or a future TGAI local-server frontend.

REFERENCE-ONLY local-desktop candidate. Ollama currently exposes Qwen3.5 9B at about 6.6 GB with 256K context plus text/image input, tools and thinking. It is a useful lighter bridge between browser-sized models and 20+ GB coding-workstation models.

models.display_name: Qwen3.5 27B Coding · Emerging Local Coding Reference
models.good_for_text: REFERENCE-ONLY emerging coding variant. Ollama's current Qwen3.5 tag set includes 27B coding-oriented packages, including platform-specific quantizations. Treat as a local-workstation research target rather than a WebLLM/browser-loadable model, and verify the exact package/runtime before recommending it.

models.display_name: Qwen3.5 35B-A3B Coding · Emerging MoE Coding Reference
models.good_for_text: REFERENCE-ONLY emerging MoE coding target. Current Ollama tags expose coding-oriented 35B-A3B packages in several quantizations. This belongs in the heavyweight local coding-workstation track, not the browser track.
